title: History’s Losers, Still Banging.
dek: Neanderthals didn’t lose. They married in. A scoreboard of history’s upright losers, ranked by one question: did they hook up with the winners?
summary: How Neanderthals, Denisovans and ‘ghost’ populations survive as DNA in living humans, ranked against extinct human relatives who left no trace.

blocks.text: The official story: around 40,000 years ago, a better-organized species of human walked into Europe and the Neanderthals walked out of history. Game over. Thanks for playing.
Except they’re still here. They’re in you. If your family tree has branches outside Africa, roughly 1 to 2 percent of your DNA came from a Neanderthal.
They lost the war. They won the bedroom. And the cousins who never got a date? Those are the real losers.¹
of the entire Neanderthal genome is still walking around, split up among living humans. Mostly buying oat milk.

blocks.title: Plot Twist: It Went Both Ways

blocks.text: They had our Y chromosome. Modern-human DNA flowed into Neanderthals in waves from ~250,000 years ago. By the end, Neanderthal men carried a sapiens Y. The losers had our surname and our grandmother’s mitochondria. [1]
Mostly Neanderthal dads, human moms. A Feb. 2026 study in Science found 62% extra modern-human DNA on Neanderthal X chromosomes. One study. Watch this space. [2]
Meet Denny. Neanderthal mom, Denisovan dad: the only first-generation hybrid of two archaic groups ever found. The losers were dating each other, too. [1]
² Neanderthals never lived in Africa. Their DNA got there the way your mom’s casserole dish ends up at my house: somebody carried it back. [E.G.]
³ Banging the winners was necessary. It was not sufficient. This also describes my twenties. [H.C.]

blocks.text: Other Losers Who Banged Their Way to Victory
Extinct, but it doesn’t mean that their gene pool is erased.

items: Cave bear → brown bear: 0.9–2.4%. Extinct ~24,000 years. Still riding around in living brown bears. [1]
Mystery mammoth → Columbian: ~50%. A lineage nobody knew existed is half of America’s iconic mammoth. [1]
Mountain weed → corn: ~20%. Highland teosinte is in every modern maize genome. [1]
Goatgrass → bread wheat: 1 of 3. Wheat’s genomes. A weed crashed the party ~10,000 years ago and brought the gluten. [0]
Polar bear → ABC Islands brown bears: up to 8.8%. Polar bear DNA in Alaskan brown bears. One-way traffic. [1]
Wolves + dogs → eastern coyotes: 26% / 10%. Wolf / dog. Wiped out of the East, still riding inside the coyotes. [0]
Red wolf → Galveston canids: ~40 yrs. After red wolves vanished from Texas, their “ghost” genes turned up on the island. [1]
Aurochs + steppe bison → wisent: 2 extinct parents, one cow-bison hybrid lineage, and today’s European bison. [1–2]

blocks.text: Bonus · The reverse loser: Near Eastern pigs arrived in Europe and got absorbed by local wild boar so thoroughly that European pigs kept 4% or less of their ancestry. The invaders lost by banging. [0–1]
History belongs to whoever keeps the files. Turns out the Neanderthals kept theirs in the safest archive on Earth: you.
The Real Losers Are the Ones Who Didn’t Hook Up.
